verdict.rationale: Ubuntu Desktop is explicitly designed for open installation on user-chosen hardware: docs show installing in place of Windows or dual-boot, support for older hardware, Raspberry Pi, and NVIDIA driver installation instructions, all without proprietary lock-in to a vendor ecosystem. Community threads corroborate real-world driver flexibility though note occasional friction with proprietary GPU blobs, which is a hardware-vendor issue rather than an Ubuntu lock-in issue. Missing for 10: no independent benchmark of hardware compatibility breadth or a broader survey of supported device diversity beyond Pi/older PCs/NVIDIA.
